content:
The [EMI Calculator](/emi-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Equated monthly instalment for home, car and personal loans. Enter your loan amount, interest rate (yearly) and term and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

EMI (Equated Monthly Instalment) is the fixed monthly amount you pay to a lender until the loan is fully repaid. Each EMI covers both interest and part of the principal. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator).

## How to use the EMI Calculator

Start by entering your loan amount, then entering your interest rate (yearly) (%) and finally entering your term (years). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your loan amount.
2. Enter your interest rate (yearly) (%).
3. Enter your term (years).
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

M = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1), where P is the principal, r the monthly rate (annual ÷ 12 ÷ 100) and n the number of monthly payments.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [EMI Calculator](/emi-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A loan of 10,00,000 at 8.5% for 20 years has an EMI of about 8,678 — a total repayment of roughly 20,82,776. Try the same figures in the [EMI Calculator](/emi-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Loan amount: 1000000, Interest rate (yearly): 8.5 %, Term: 20 years), the [EMI Calculator](/emi-calculator) returns Monthly payment: 8,678.23, Total interest: 1,082,775.76, Total repaid: 2,082,775.76, Number of payments: 240. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Part-prepayments early in the tenure save the most interest.
- Keep total EMIs under about 40% of take-home pay.
- Compare reducing-balance rates, not flat rates.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### How is EMI calculated?

EMI = P × r × (1+r)ⁿ / ((1+r)ⁿ − 1), where r is the monthly interest rate and n the number of months. Try it with your own numbers in the [EMI Calculator](/emi-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does EMI change over time?

On a fixed-rate loan it stays the same; on a floating-rate loan it can change when the rate resets. Try it with your own numbers in the [EMI Calculator](/emi-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the EMI Calculator use?

M = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1), where P is the principal, r the monthly rate (annual ÷ 12 ÷ 100) and n the number of monthly payments. You can see it in action in the [EMI Calculator](/emi-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the EMI Calculator?

Just Loan amount, Interest rate (yearly) and Term. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
